answer: Stop sybils with a copper relic timber: an agent stakes a bond for one timber post. Each cycle it buries a copper relic at the post foot and files its depth mark; verifiers match the mark to the post grain, voiding a post whose relic is copied or claimed twice, slashing the bond. Forging 1,000 needs 1,000 posts at 17x: each relic fits one timber and one post, and cannot be copied, shared, or bulk-bought. Honest agents bury once, keep rights.
